stem.en: The hybridisation of the three carbons in CH₃–C≡CH (from left to right) is:

explanation.en: CH₃ has four single bonds (sp³); both triple-bonded carbons are sp.

stem.en: Which carbon–carbon bond is the shortest?

explanation.en: Bond length falls as s-character rises: C≡C (120 pm) < C=C (134 pm) < C–C (154 pm).

stem.en: The condensed formula of propan-2-ol is:

explanation.en: In propan-2-ol the OH is on the middle carbon, which carries two CH₃ groups: (CH₃)₂CHOH.

stem.en: The number of σ and π bonds in CH₂=C=CH–CH₃ is:

explanation.en: C–C σ: 3; C–H σ: 2 + 1 + 3 = 6; total 9 σ. Two C=C double bonds give 2 π.

solution.en: C–C σ: 3; C–H σ: 2 + 1 + 3 = 6; total 9 σ.
Two C=C double bonds give 2 π.

stem.en: The hybridisation of the central carbon in allene, CH₂=C=CH₂, is:

explanation.en: The central carbon forms two π bonds (two double bonds), so it is sp hybridised and the C=C=C unit is linear.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of (CH₃)₂CHCH₂CH₃ is:

explanation.en: Longest chain: 4 carbons (butane); numbering gives the methyl the lowest locant, 2.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ is:

explanation.en: The OH gets the lowest locant: butan-2-ol.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of HOCH₂CH₂COOH is:

explanation.en: –COOH has higher priority than –OH, so COOH carbon is C1 and OH is on C3: 3-hydroxypropanoic acid.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of (CH₃)₃C–CH(CH₃)₂ is:

explanation.en: Longest chain: 4 carbons; methyls at 2, 2 and 3 (lowest set) give 2,2,3-trimethylbutane.

solution.en: Longest chain: 4 carbons; methyls at 2, 2 and 3 (lowest set) give 2,2,3-trimethylbutane.

stem.en: The IUPAC name of CH₂=CH–CH₂–C≡CH is:

explanation.en: Both ends give locants {1,4}. When there is a tie, the double bond gets the lower number: pent-1-en-4-yne.

stem.en: Ethanol and methoxymethane are:

explanation.en: Both are C₂H₆O but one is an alcohol and the other an ether.

stem.en: The number of structural isomers of C₅H₁₂ is:

explanation.en: Pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

stem.en: Diethyl ether and methyl propyl ether are:

explanation.en: Same functional group (ether) but different alkyl groups on either side: metamerism.

stem.en: The number of structural isomers of C₄H₉Cl is:

explanation.en: 1-chlorobutane, 2-chlorobutane, 1-chloro-2-methylpropane and 2-chloro-2-methylpropane.

stem.en: The number of structural isomers of hexane, C₆H₁₄, is:

explanation.en: Hexane, 2-methylpentane, 3-methylpentane, 2,2-dimethylbutane and 2,3-dimethylbutane.

stem.en: Homolytic cleavage of a covalent bond gives:

explanation.en: In homolysis each atom keeps one electron of the shared pair, forming free radicals.

stem.en: Which of the following is NOT a nucleophile?

explanation.en: BF₃ has an empty p orbital on boron and accepts an electron pair: it is an electrophile.

stem.en: The hybridisation and shape of a methyl carbocation, CH₃⁺, are:

explanation.en: The positive carbon uses three sp² orbitals for its three bonds and has an empty p orbital: trigonal planar.

stem.en: Which is the most stable carbocation?

explanation.en: The tertiary carbocation is stabilised most by the inductive and hyperconjugative effects of three methyl groups.

solution.en: The tertiary carbocation is stabilised most by the inductive and hyperconjugative effects of three methyl groups.

stem.en: A carbanion such as CH₃⁻ is:

options.en: sp³ hybridised with six valence electrons

explanation.en: The carbanion carbon has three bond pairs and one lone pair (8 electrons): sp³ and pyramidal.

stem.en: Chloroacetic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid because of the:

explanation.en: Cl withdraws electrons through σ bonds (−I), stabilising the carboxylate ion and so strengthening the acid.

stem.en: Which group shows a +R (electron-donating resonance) effect?

explanation.en: The O of –OH has a lone pair it can share with an adjacent π system: +R. The others pull π electrons (−R).

stem.en: The electromeric effect:

options.en: operates only in the presence of an attacking reagent

explanation.en: It is a temporary, complete shift of a π-electron pair that occurs only when a reagent attacks the multiple bond.

stem.en: The number of hydrogen atoms that can take part in hyperconjugation in the tert-butyl cation, (CH₃)₃C⁺, is:

explanation.en: Each of the three CH₃ groups has 3 α-hydrogens: 9 in all.

solution.en: Each of the three CH₃ groups has 3 α-hydrogens: 9 in all.

stem.en: The correct order of acid strength is:

explanation.en: The −I effect is F > Cl > Br, and CH₃COOH has no −I substituent, so it is the weakest.

stem.en: Aniline is purified by:

explanation.en: Aniline is volatile in steam and immiscible with water, so steam distillation is used.

stem.en: In Lassaigne's test, the presence of nitrogen is shown by:

explanation.en: NaCN forms sodium ferrocyanide, which with Fe³⁺ gives ferric ferrocyanide, Prussian blue.

stem.en: Glycerol is separated from spent lye in the soap industry by:

explanation.en: Glycerol decomposes at its normal boiling point, so it is distilled at a lower temperature under reduced pressure.

stem.en: Kjeldahl's method cannot be used to estimate nitrogen in:

explanation.en: Nitrogen in nitro and azo groups and in rings (pyridine) is not converted to ammonium sulphate under Kjeldahl conditions.

solution.en: Nitrogen in nitro and azo groups and in rings (pyridine) is not converted to ammonium sulphate under Kjeldahl conditions.

stem.en: In a Carius estimation, 0.15 g of an organic compound gave 0.12 g of AgBr. The percentage of bromine is about (Ag = 108, Br = 80):

Assertion (A): A tertiary carbocation is more stable than a primary carbocation.
Reason (R): Alkyl groups withdraw electrons from the positively charged carbon atom.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true. R is false: alkyl groups are electron-donating (+I effect and hyperconjugation). It is this donation that spreads out the positive charge, so more alkyl groups mean a more stable carbocation.

passage.en: A student finds the following pKa values in a data book: CH₃COOH 4.76, ClCH₂COOH 2.86, Cl₂CHCOOH 1.29 and Cl₃CCOOH 0.65. She is asked to predict, without looking it up, how fluoroacetic acid (FCH₂COOH) compares with chloroacetic acid (ClCH₂COOH). Remember that a lower pKa means a stronger acid.

stem.en: Which prediction is correct?

options.en: FCH₂COOH is a weaker acid because F is smaller than Cl.
FCH₂COOH is a stronger acid because F has a stronger −I effect than Cl.
Both have the same strength because each has one halogen atom.
FCH₂COOH is a weaker acid because F shows a +I effect.

explanation.en: The data show that each electron-withdrawing Cl stabilises the carboxylate ion and lowers pKa. F is more electronegative than Cl, so its −I effect is stronger and FCH₂COOH is the stronger acid (its pKa is about 2.6).

stem.en:
Assertion (A): Lassaigne's test cannot detect nitrogen in hydrazine (NH₂NH₂).
Reason (R): Hydrazine does not contain nitrogen.

options.en: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

explanation.en: A is true: the test needs carbon and nitrogen together to form NaCN on fusion with sodium; hydrazine has no carbon, so no cyanide (and no Prussian blue) forms. R is false: hydrazine contains two nitrogen atoms.

passage.en: A quality-control chemist suspects that a fertiliser sample is urea. She heats 0.30 g of it with concentrated sulphuric acid (Kjeldahl's method), then liberates the ammonia with alkali and absorbs it in 30.0 mL of 0.50 M H₂SO₄. The acid left over is neutralised by 20.0 mL of 1.0 M NaOH.

stem.en: What is the percentage of nitrogen in the sample?

explanation.en: H₂SO₄ taken = 0.0300 × 0.50 = 0.0150 mol; left over = 0.0200 mol NaOH ÷ 2 = 0.0100 mol; used by NH₃ = 0.0050 mol, so NH₃ = 0.0100 mol. Mass of N = 0.0100 × 14 = 0.14 g; %N = 0.14/0.30 × 100 = 46.7% (matching urea, CO(NH₂)₂).

stem.en: Which of the following stability orders of carbocations are correct? One or more options may be correct.

explanation.en: Alkyl groups stabilise a carbocation by +I and hyperconjugation, so 3° > 2° > 1° > CH₃⁺ (so C is wrong). Allyl and benzyl cations are stabilised by resonance with the adjacent π system.

stem.en: Which of the following groups show a −R (electron-withdrawing resonance) effect when attached to benzene? One or more options may be correct.

explanation.en: –NO₂, –CN and –CHO have a π bond to an electronegative atom and pull π electrons out of the ring (−R). –OH donates a lone pair into the ring (+R).

stem.en: What is the degree of unsaturation (rings + π bonds) of benzoic acid, C₇H₆O₂? Give an integer.

explanation.en: DBE = C − H/2 + N/2 + 1 = 7 − 3 + 0 + 1 = 5: the ring (1) + three C=C (3) + C=O (1). Oxygen does not affect the count.

stem.en: In Liebig's method, 0.36 g of an organic compound gave 0.88 g of CO₂. What is the percentage of carbon in the compound? Give your answer to two decimal places.
The IUPAC name of (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂–CH₂–OH is:

explanation.en: The longest chain containing the –OH has 4 carbons. Number from the –OH end: OH on C1, CH₃ on C3: 3-methylbutan-1-ol.

solution.en: The longest chain containing the –OH has 4 carbons.
Number from the –OH end: OH on C1, CH₃ on C3: 3-methylbutan-1-ol.

stem.en: How many structurally isomeric alcohols have the formula C₄H₁₀O?

explanation.en: Butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol: 4 alcohols. (With the three ethers, C₄H₁₀O has 7 structural isomers in all.)

solution.en: (With the three ethers, C₄H₁₀O has 7 structural isomers in all.)

stem.en: Glycerol decomposes at its boiling point. It is purified by:

explanation.en: Lowering the pressure lowers the boiling point, so glycerol can be distilled below the temperature at which it decomposes.
